title: When the Salt Falls Revisited
premise: Elodie Blackwood has spent two decades as a charm-seller in Saltmere, a city where magic is outlawed, hiding his true role: keeper of the Undergate, a sealed door between the human world and the drowned realm of the Tidewrought. When the crown's witch-hunters begin executing anyone with the gift, Elodie's warding charms start failing one by one, and he realizes the gate beneath his shop is already leaking—and something on the other side remembers him by name. Hunted by Inquisitor Vane, who suspects what Elodie carries, and aided by a runaway tide-priestess named Maren and a disgraced royal cartographer, Elodie must decide whether to re-seal the gate with his own memories as payment or open it and let the exiled Tidewrought return home. At the climax, Elodie learns the ancient war began because his own ancestor stole the Tidewrought's inheritance—their names—and that only returning them can end the cycle. He gives up his own name to the tide, unmaking himself as keeper but freeing both worlds; the book ends with Maren rebuilding Saltmere's harbor while a nameless stranger sells small charms by the sea, smiling at customers whose faces he almost remembers.
about_author: Sebastian Okonkwo is a former marine archivist who spent years cataloguing shipwreck salvage off the western coast before turning to fiction full-time. His work blends tidal folklore, quiet magic, and stories about the things families refuse to pass down.

chapters.title: Charms for Ordinary Weather
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A day in his cluttered charm shop in Saltmere: selling luck-knots to fishermen, hiding real magic inside harmless trinkets. Establishes his careful invisibility and loneliness. Emotional beat: the ache of a life built entirely around concealment.

chapters.title: The Proclamation
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Royal criers announce the Gift-Hunt: anyone found with magic will be tried and burned. Elodie watches neighbors he's charmed for years turn their eyes on each other. Emotional beat: fear curdling into the realization that his safety was always borrowed.

chapters.title: What the Cellar Keeps
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. He descends to the Undergate for its monthly inspection and finds saltwater seeping through seams that have held for twenty years. Something knocks from the other side—three slow taps, like a greeting. Emotional beat: dread mixed with an unwelcome flicker of recognition.

chapters.title: Maren of the Drowned Choir
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. A young tide-priestess arrives in Saltmere disguised as a fish-gutter, fleeing the purge of her coastal order. She senses the leaking gate within hours of entering the city. Emotional beat: desperate hope—she believes the gate opening might save her people.

chapters.title: Inquisitor Vane Pays a Call
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Vane, soft-spoken and terrifyingly thorough, buys a charm from Elodie and lingers, asking questions about 'old families' and 'inherited gifts.' Elodie lies well, but Vane leaves a marked coin behind. Emotional beat: the hunter's patience versus the keeper's practiced calm.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Error
chapters.summary: Tobias Wrenn's POV. A disgraced royal mapmaker notices that official charts omit an entire district of old Saltmere—the district built over the Undergate. He brings his findings to the crown, not knowing what he's handing them. Emotional beat: guilt foreshadowed; a good man about to do harm.

chapters.title: Salt in the Well Water
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The city's wells turn brackish; children dream of singing under the streets. Maren traces the contamination to the gate and confronts Elodie in his shop, naming him keeper. Emotional beat: collision of two people who want opposite things from the same door.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Small Lies
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV, with flashback. We learn how Elodie inherited keepership from his mother, who sealed the gate after the last Tidewrought war and paid for it with her memories. Emotional beat: grief reframed—he finally understands why she never spoke of the past.

chapters.title: The Marked Coin
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The coin Vane left begins humming whenever magic is used nearby; half of Saltmere's hidden practitioners are arrested in a single night. Elodie must choose which neighbors to warn, knowing every warning draws Vane closer. Emotional beat: survivor's guilt sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Names Are Currency
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. She reveals the Tidewrought theology: humans long ago stole the Tidewrought's true names, which is why they were exiled and why the gate hungers. Names can be returned—but only willingly, and only by a keeper's line. Emotional beat: wonder shadowed by the price she's asking.

chapters.title: Vane's Ledger
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. Inside the Inquisition, we see Vane's private obsession: his sister was executed as a witch twenty years ago, and he hunts not from zealotry but from a need to prove the gift is a curse worth erasing. Emotional beat: making the antagonist heartbreakingly human.

chapters.title: The Knocking Grows Louder
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The gate's leaks flood the cellar; through the water, Elodie hears his own childhood nickname spoken in his mother's voice. He realizes the thing beyond isn't a monster—it's the exiled dead, including perhaps part of her. Emotional beat: longing warring with duty.

chapters.title: An Unlikely Alliance
chapters.summary: Tobias's POV. Tobias, wracked by guilt over his map, seeks out Elodie to confess and offer help navigating the crown's archives. The three allies form a fragile plan: find the stolen names in the royal vault before Vane does. Emotional beat: cautious trust among strangers bound by secrets.

chapters.title: Into the Vault of Quiet Things
chapters.summary: Elodie and Maren's alternating POV. They infiltrate the palace archive during a state funeral and discover the names aren't scrolls—they're bound into the city's foundation stones. Saltmere itself was built as a prison. Emotional beat: horror at realizing home is a cage.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Archive
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. Tobias is caught leaving the archive; under threat of execution, he gives up Elodie's name and shop. Vane doesn't gloat—he looks almost relieved to finally have someone to stop. Emotional beat: betrayal born of fear, not malice.

chapters.title: The Burning of Charm Row
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Vane raids the shop district; hidden practitioners are dragged out, and Elodie's cellar—gate exposed—is sealed with soldiers. Elodie escapes through a drain with only his mother's iron key. Emotional beat: rage and loss; the invisible life burned to ash.

chapters.title: What My Mother Paid
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Hiding in the sea caves, Elodie uses the key to speak through the gate and learns the full truth: his mother didn't seal the gate to imprison the Tidewrought—she sealed it to buy time until someone brave enough to return the names came along. That someone was always meant to be him. Emotional beat: inheritance transformed from burden into invitation.

chapters.title: The Tide Rises in Saltmere
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. With the gate breached, the sea climbs the streets; the Tidewrought dead walk the flooded avenues, gentle and grieving, asking citizens for their names back. Panic spreads, and Vane orders the district drowned with fire instead. Emotional beat: awe curdling into catastrophe.

chapters.title: Three Taps on the Door
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie returns to the gate through the flooding city, past burning ships and singing water, and reaches the door as Vane confronts him. Instead of fighting, Elodie shows Vane the truth of his sister's name—she was Tidewrought-touched, and her name is held beyond the gate too. Emotional beat: the climax pivots on mercy, not violence.

chapters.title: The Return of Names
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Vane stands down and helps hold the gate open. Elodie speaks the stolen names back to the tide, each one costing him a memory of his own, ending with his own name given last. The Tidewrought cross over—not as invaders but as the returning dead, at peace. Emotional beat: sacrificial transcendence; grief and release braided together.

chapters.title: A City That Remembers Differently
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Weeks later: the floods recede, the hunt dissolves, and Saltmere rebuilds with tide-priests and charm-sellers working openly. Maren tends a small shrine to the nameless keeper, telling his story so it won't be lost again. Emotional beat: mourning that has learned to be gratitude.

chapters.title: Small Charms by the Sea
chapters.summary: Nameless stranger's POV, close third. A man with no past runs a stall near the rebuilt harbor, selling luck-knots and weather-charms. When Maren passes, he smiles without knowing why, and she buys a charm neither of them needs. Emotional beat: belonging found not in memory but in chosen presence—a quiet, hopeful close.
